tool.title: Where to drop a file — the queue's upload URL
tool.description: Compose the forge URL a person can drop a file at, from the layer's own declaration: the `uploads` graph's directory, resolved against the ROOT its scope names, expressed relative to the repository, and appended to the origin remote as GitHub's `/upload/<branch>/<path>`. Every failure is NAMED and no URL is guessed — no declaration, no declared `uploads` graph, a declared queue absent from disk, no `origin` remote, and a non-github.com remote each return a reason and a remedy instead. The declared path is relative to the LAYER and a forge URL needs it relative to the REPOSITORY, so pasting the declared path can mint a 404.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.description: The branch the upload form targets. Defaults to `main`; pass the working branch to send somebody to a pull request's head instead, so the upload lands on a commit CI judges.

outputs.name: url
outputs.description: The upload URL on stdout, exit 0 — or, on stderr and exit 1, the reason it could not be composed and the remedy for that reason. Never a guessed URL: a URL is believed, and somebody sent to a wrong one cannot tell it from an empty directory.

selection.when: You are about to tell somebody where to put a file, in any channel. Reach for it every time, not only when unsure: a hand-written path breaks silently when a directory moves. It also answers "which queue" when a checkout declares more than one (one per layer): the answer is whichever layer root you pass, never a literal.
selection.limits: It answers WHERE, and nothing else. It does not upload, does not check whether the person has write access, and cannot tell you which of several declared queues should own a given file — that is undecided and `upload-routes` says so rather than picking. The `/upload/<branch>/<path>` form is GitHub's, so another forge gets a named refusal rather than a guess. And the URL it hands back opens the route with the FEWEST guarantees: the web form has no working tree, so no pre-commit hook and no generator run happen on it, and everything `upload-routes` lists has to be discharged afterwards from a checkout.
selection.cost: One read of the declaration and one of the git remote; no network at run time and nothing installed.
